units.text: Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python reads HTML input and parses it into a standards-based DOM tree using HTMLDocument.parse, HTMLDocument.parse_fragment, and tree.parse_html. It writes serialized markup output using serialise and XMLSerializer. It applies CSS by attaching CSSStyleSheet objects and resolving computed styles via ComputedStyleDeclaration, supports CSS selector matching with aspose_html.css.select, and detects byte-stream encoding with detect_encoding. It handles URL parsing and query parameter manipulation with URL and URLSearchParams, and provides optional JavaScript execution through JSContext backed by QuickJS.

It parses HTML strings, bytes, fragments, and files into a DOM document using aspose_html.HTMLDocument.parse, aspose_html.HTMLDocument.parse_fragment, and aspose_html.HTMLDocument.load, while aspose_html.tree.parse_html and aspose_html.tree.TreeBuilder provide lower-level control over the tokenization and tree-construction process.

It builds, inspects, and mutates DOM trees by creating and updating nodes programmatically with aspose_html.dom.Document.create_element and append_child, reading and writing element attributes, classes, datasets, inline styles, and text content, and querying documents by ID, tag name, class name, and selector-oriented helpers such as get_element_by_id, get_elements_by_tag_name, TreeWalker, NodeIterator, and Range.

It matches CSS selectors and stylesheets against elements and resolves the cascade—including specificity, inline-vs-author rules, !important, and inheritance—with aspose_html.dom.Element.get_computed_style, while the CSSOM surface provided by aspose_html.cssom.CSSStyleSheet, aspose_html.cssom.CSSStyleRule, aspose_html.cssom.CSSMediaRule, and aspose_html.dom.ComputedStyleDeclaration models stylesheets structurally.

It validates and manipulates URLs with aspose_html.url.URL, reads and edits query strings with aspose_html.url.URLSearchParams, and detects byte-stream character encodings using BOM and content sniffing with aspose_html.encoding.detect_encoding.

It executes JavaScript against a parsed DOM through aspose_html.js.JSContext, an optional QuickJS-backed bridge exposing DOM read-only proxies to script code, requiring the js extra dependency quickjs>=1.19,<2.

It implements the WHATWG tokenization and tree-construction algorithms directly through aspose_html.tokenizer.Tokenizer and aspose_html.tokenizer.StartTagToken, enabling callers who need low-level control over the parsing process.

It exposes specialized HTML element classes such as aspose_html.dom.HTMLInputElement, aspose_html.dom.HTMLTableElement, and aspose_html.dom.HTMLMediaElement, each providing element-specific properties defined by their HTML interface.

It serializes complete documents, fragments, and individual elements back to an HTML string using aspose_html.serialise or aspose_html.XMLSerializer, with aspose_html.serialiser.outer_html providing additional control over the output format.
Parse an HTML string into a DOM, locate an element by its ID, create a new paragraph, set its text content, append it to the container, and serialize the updated subtree.
Build a DOM with styled elements, attach an external CSS style sheet, and query the computed style property of an element to verify the applied rule.
The following workflows demonstrate URL manipulation, element querying, encoding detection, and tokenization.
Modify URL search parameters.
Query elements by tag name.
Detect character encoding from bytes.
Tokenize HTML input.

Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python provides the HTMLDocument class as the primary entry point for parsing HTML into a Document tree. It supports loading from files, parsing full documents, and parsing HTML fragments.
The HTMLDocument class provides parse, parse_fragment, and load methods to construct a DOM tree from HTML strings or files.

The Document class serves as the root of the DOM tree and provides methods such as create_element, append_child, get_element_by_id, and get_elements_by_tag_name to build and query the tree, with Element and NodeList supporting node manipulation and collection access.
The CSSStyleSheet class represents a CSS stylesheet and works with CSSStyleRule and ComputedStyleDeclaration to manage styles and computed style information for elements.
The URL class provides URL parsing and component access, with URLSearchParams handling query string operations.
The detect_encoding function analyzes byte streams to determine encoding and decode HTML content.
The JSContext class provides a JavaScript execution environment backed by QuickJS and integrates with the DOM.
The Tokenizer class implements the WHATWG HTML tokeniser and produces tokens such as StartTagToken during parsing.
The serialise function and XMLSerializer class convert DOM nodes back into HTML or XML markup strings.

Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python reads and writes HTML documents, parses CSS, and provides a DOM API with CSS selector matching, layout structure construction, and optional JavaScript execution via an external engine.

CSS selector matching supports the core CSS Selectors Level 3 grammar, but several dynamic and legacy pseudo-classes are out of scope and raise NotImplementedError in the matcher and parser, and single-colon legacy pseudo-element forms are not parsed.
CSSRule.type and CSSRule.css_text are not implemented; concrete rule subclasses such as CSSStyleRule and CSSMediaRule expose their own real properties instead.
Form constraint validation and HTMLImageElement.decode() are present on the API surface but not yet implemented.
The library builds internal layout structures using BoxNode and PageFragment with skia-python for text-run metrics but does not yet expose a public API for rendering documents to an image or PDF.

JavaScript execution via JSContext requires the optional quickjs extra and exposes a read-only DOM proxy to script code; its dynamic import() bridge is not implemented, though static module registration via ModuleRegistry works.
